title: test
text: Context : Car dependence is a feedback loop. Accessibility by car spreads activities out: dispersed development requires more driving, and more driving generates demand for more road capacity. Transport-side accounts (source) and land-use accounts (Solow, Arnott and MacKinnon, Newman and Kenworthy) describe the same loop. The land-use account matters most here because street space is a zero-sum allocation. Road space given to cars is taken from housing, shops, and public space.
